content.title: 10 Things You Only Notice About America After Leaving
content.text: there are many ways that moving abroad in my early 20s has changed my life, but something I didn’t expect is how much it has changed the way I see America. somethings make me more appreciative, some more concerned (of which I highlight more in this video). and I don't mean to bash on America or romanticize other countries - especially Korea, which I refer to a lot, since that is where I've been living. like I mention at the end, the reason why I am concerned is because I do love this country and see real room for ways it can change. if you’re American, I’m curious what hit you the hardest when you traveled or lived abroad? and if you’re not American, what are the things about the U.S. that stand out to you immediately - or has the way you viewed your own country changed since traveling or living abroad?
